espn-604011.headline: Italy get a second go at the side that made it seven
beats: Fiji won 21–16 in Udine on 21 November after Italy had led 13–7 at half-time. The finals draw sends both sides straight back at each other, this time at Allianz Stadium, for 11th place.

Italy's run of defeats began against Wales at the end of the Six Nations. It includes 66 conceded to South Africa and 57 to Australia, but the last two were lost by five points each. Forwards coach Roberto Santamaria blamed the breakdown and execution against a side he called within reach.

Italy lose flyhalf Domingo Miotti and prop Simone Ferrari to injury, while Garbisi and Lynagh return. Fiji have changed their front row and both their halfback and centre pairings. Win by 16 or more and Italy go above Fiji and Japan to 10th in the world.
Italy's next game is Scotland away in February. Fiji's is a World Cup pool match against Spain next October, which is a long time to sit on a loss.

espn-604012.headline: Ireland can reach world No 1 by finishing fifth
beats: This is the fifth-place final, North 3rd against South 3rd. Ireland won five of six pool games and finished a point behind England. Any win here takes them above South Africa to first in the world.

They do it without captain Dan Sheehan. He was banned for two weeks after his croc roll on Marco van Staden, in the 20–17 win over South Africa, was upgraded to red. Tadhg Beirne leads the side and Nick Timoney starts at No 8. Jacob Stockdale, absent all autumn, replaces the injured Mack Hansen.
Australia came within two points in July, losing 31–33 at home. Since then they have conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand and beaten Wales by three.
Ticket sales are sluggish enough that Twickenham could be half empty to watch it.

espn-604013.headline: Wales rest the big hitters for a side they barely beat
beats: Three weeks ago in Cardiff, Japan were level on tries until Josh Adams scored in the 69th minute. Wales won 28–21. Steve Tandy has still promised to rotate for this 9th-place final at Allianz Stadium, with next year's World Cup in mind, and outside-half Dan Edwards is out with an ankle injury.

Japan have not held a scoreline since. England put 78 on them, then Scotland 67 with eleven tries in Edinburgh. Wales beat New Zealand and lost to Australia by three. Eleven of their players started all three of those games.

This is the fifth meeting in 16 months, so nobody will be surprised by anybody. Only a Japan win by 16 or more lifts them above Wales in the world rankings, which on recent evidence is not the likeliest result.
Wales's next game is France away in February, in a Six Nations with no room for trial runs. This is the last chance to look at the squad's depth, against the side that took them to the 69th minute.

espn-604014.headline: Third place, and a third straight win England have never had
beats: England beat New Zealand 37–12 at Allianz Stadium a week ago, New Zealand's record defeat against them. Do it again in the third-place final and it is the first time England have ever beaten New Zealand in three successive Tests.

New Zealand have lost two straight, conceding 35 to Wales and then 37 here. Schalk Burger says England "bullied" them while they ignored the gain-line, and offers the fix in four words: "Gain-line is king."
England have made five changes, with Tommy Freeman passed fit. Win by 16 or more, as they managed by 25 last week, and England go to 1st in the world rankings, above South Africa, Ireland and France.
New Zealand Rugby says Dave Rennie stays whatever happens. His next Test after this is Chile in October 2027, a long time to sit on another result like last week's.

espn-604015.headline: Seventh place, decided by whoever is left standing
beats: Scotland are without their captain, Sione Tuipulotu, and Matt Fagerson has a jaw injury from the 67–5 win over Japan. Argentina have made six squad changes after a November of injuries, plus a red card for Mayco Vivas against France.
Scotland's back row is short enough that Liam McConnell, who scored a hat-trick against Japan on his second Test start, may get another go.
Scotland won the July meeting in Cordoba 47–38. Since then Argentina have conceded 42 to Ireland and 45 to France. Even so, a win by 16 or more would lift them above Scotland into sixth in the world.
Scotland play Italy in February. Argentina's next Test is Canada at the World Cup in October, which is a long time to sit on eighth.

espn-604016.headline: Seven scrum penalties, and France still won by two
beats: That was Paris on 13 November, 21–19, with South Africa holding 55 per cent of the ball and 58 per cent of the territory. They also lost it 16 times. The rematch is the Nations Championship final, at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham.

South Africa have lost since, 20–17 to Ireland in Dublin. Schalk Burger says they have "only got a maul and a scrum at the minute", which is a complaint and also the plan. Pieter-Steph du Toit, 34 and twice World Player of the Year, is out with a "niggle".

France arrive on five straight wins, the last 45–17 over Argentina with seven tries. They come without Grégory Alldritt, who has a calf injury. Win again and they go to first in the world, above South Africa.
Lose, and France will not need the review to tell them where it went wrong.
